In Banja Luka there were trucks waiting for them, and they transported them to Belgrade. In Belgrade, there were already transportation means to move them --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes. You now apparently arrive at the point that I'm interested in. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: EMIN TESKEREDZIC
utterances.text: And when they arrived, they wanted to move them to Kosovo. But this is where they reacted and objected. This is what she told me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, the conclusion that it was planned and organised therefore, but please correct me when I'm wrong, that conclusion was drawn on the basis of a group of people coming and shouting, The Ustashas are coming, they're going to slaughter everybody. And then having moved to Banja Luka, trucks were waiting for them and to transport them to Belgrade. Is there any other fact she told you which supports the conclusion that it was all planned and organised?

utterances.speaker: EMIN TESKEREDZIC
utterances.text: Well, these were sufficient reasons on which I could base my conclusion that everything was planned and organised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You also said that she told you that 99 per cent of the people had left that area before the Croats returned to the territory of the former Krajina. Did she give you any further details as to when they left or whether they returned ever after?

utterances.speaker: EMIN TESKEREDZIC
utterances.text: She did not mention any details, but people did come back. I spoke to them. They were around. She was one of those who came back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And she is Serb; is that what I --

utterances.speaker: EMIN TESKEREDZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you for those answers. Have the questions by the Bench triggered any need? Mr. Kay, thank you very much for D1023 which places Mr. Frkic clearly in the garrison command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: One matter arising from what His Honour asked you, and it concerns the request that General Cermak made to you, and you said that he never asked you anything that was unreasonable and you had no occasion to -- not to follow any request. Looking at it from other way, if had you refused any request by Mr. Cermak, could he have disciplined you.

utterances.speaker: EMIN TESKEREDZIC
utterances.text: Well, in theory, yes. But there was simply no need for that. I was a volunteer, so my status was much more liberal, so to say, than it would have been if I was mobilized or part of the military establishment. But I was a scientist, so they treated me in a different way, not so strictly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There are no further questions for you, Mr. Teskeredzic. Therefore, this concludes your testimony. I'd like to thank you very much for coming this long way to The Hague and for having answered the questions that were put to you by the parties and by the Bench, and I would wish you -- I would like to wish you a safe return home again. Mr. Usher, could you escort Mr. Teskeredzic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to move into private session for a short while.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. For the witness to appear tomorrow, what we have heard is an estimate from the Defence as to the time needed for examination-in-chief and we have TBDs which stands for to be determined for the other parties. Since we may have a little scheduling problem tomorrow, which means that we'd have to stop a little bit earlier than usual, not later than 1.30 p.m., could I inquire with the parties whether there's any chance that we could conclude the testimony of that witness in this lesser time tomorrow? Mr. Kay, your assessment was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: My assessment was half a session and my assessment from what I've been seeing of cross-examination on the issues, that probably we would be able to complete him in -- in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could I ask the other Defence teams whether they would support this estimate and this assessment given by Mr. Kay in view of the TBDs still being there. Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I don't anticipate having more than 20 minutes, if that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: By all means, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr President, we would have a little over one session, so I am confident that we will be able to be finished by 1.30 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then the parties are urged to see whether we can conclude tomorrow's testimony by 1.30. Any other procedural matters to be raised at this moment? Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr, President, just with respect to the exhibits that we were discussing in private session, I offered the 65 ter number just for clerical purposes. Do we wish do get a number assigned now or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I failed to ask the Registrar to assign exhibit numbers. Or it would then be -- it's all be together now. It would be one exhibit number, that is, all of the evidence which from, what I understand, is a transcript of the Initial Appearance of Mr. Babic. It is part of Mr. Babic's plea agreement. And it's transcript of Babic testimony in the Milosevic case, both the portions tendered by the Defence and by the Prosecution, and the transcript of the testimony of Mr. Babic in the Martic case, and finally the transcript of the testimony of Mr. Babic in the Krajisnik case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, all together under 1D2977.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could you assign a number to 1D2977, and it should be D number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document becomes Exhibit D1736. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1736 is admitted into evidence. Any other procedural matter? If not, then we'll adjourn for the day, and we will resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 27th of October, 2009, 9.00, Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 27th day of October, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.
